name: Dual-token ABAC allow/deny e2e matrix through the gateway
description: To prove role-based ABAC end to end, run a Postman/newman matrix that mints TWO in-network Keycloak tokens (a viewer-only user and an editor user) and injects them as separate collection variables (viewer_token / editor_token), then asserts the matrix: editor seeds resources (201), viewer reads them (200), viewer writes are denied (403 via @OpaPreAuthorize -> role-definition-driven OPA), editor writes succeed (200/204). Crucial setup detail: the demo user must NOT hold both roles or it can't show viewer-denied-on-write — add a viewer-only realm user. Tokens are minted IN-NETWORK because APISIX validates the issuer as keycloak:8888; chained ids stay in COLLECTION scope (mx-ecc3ef). Keep per-request Authorization headers (Bearer {{viewer_token}} / {{editor_token}}) rather than a single collection-level bearer, so one collection exercises both principals.

A new e2e matrix runner seeded its fixture catalog row via psql without the ltree path column (modeled on run-tag-matrix.sh) and every gateway category create under it failed 500 fail-closed: 'cannot assign path: parent catalog:<id> has no path (broken lineage)'. run-tag-matrix.sh's pathless INSERT only appears to work because the postgres volume persists across sessions and its row already carries a path from an earlier run — on a fresh volume it would fail the same way.
resolution: Seed fixture catalog rows WITH the path (the run-pagination-matrix.sh model): INSERT ... path = CAST('catalog_' || replace('<id>','-','') AS ltree), and let the ON CONFLICT arm repair path = EXCLUDED.path for rows a prior run left NULL. Any direct-SQL row for a hierarchical type must carry its materialized path.

description: SYMPTOM: the user directory (GET /api/v1/users) fills with duplicate role-named rows (8x 'Owner', 5x 'Reader', 'Strict'...) that no identity can log in as — surfaced by the demo-UI add-member picker. ROOT CAUSE (two-part): (1) every matrix runner bootstraps the SAME shared realm users (editor/demo/viewer/outsider) but under per-matrix ROLE names ('Owner', 'PC senior'...) — conceptually wrong, the row is the identity's profile, not a matrix role; (2) /internal/bootstrap/users is find-or-create by subject and NEVER updates displayName, so whoever bootstraps a subject first names it forever — and every Keycloak realm rebuild mints new subs, orphaning ALL previous rows (they accumulate; 30 of 39 rows were orphans).
resolution: Applied 2026-07-05: (a) purged orphans by diffing app_user.subject against freshly-minted subs for the 7 realm users (team_membership FK has ON DELETE CASCADE, safe); (b) renamed outsider's row (was 'PC senior') to 'Outsider'; (c) all matrix runners now bootstrap displayName as the realm-username VARIABLE ($OWNER_USER -> 'editor'), never a role literal — only isolation-matrix Alice/Bob/Carol and synthetic pc-target-1/2 keep proper-name literals. Re-purge recipe: mint tokens in-network for all realm users, collect subs, DELETE FROM app_user WHERE subject NOT IN (live subs + synthetic fixtures). BACKLOG: make ensureUser upsert display_name so seed/matrix re-runs self-heal names.

name: Fixture registry applies to SUBJECTS too: reserve a credential-less realm account for never-provisioned probes
description: A 'never-provisioned account' e2e assertion (directory-vs-provisioned cut) is a cross-collection flake waiting: the shared usermgmt DB persists across matrix runs and users rows are never torn down, so any account another matrix (or a demo click) bootstraps arms a count=1 failure. The fix mirrors the catalog fixture-id registry, applied to subjects: (1) reserve a DEDICATED realm account (dora) whose only purpose is the probe — give her NO credentials so she structurally cannot log in or be token-minted, which is also exactly the 'never logged in' persona the headline needs; (2) register the reservation in scripts/postman/README.md (an account one matrix asserts as ABSENT must never be an account another matrix CREATES); (3) the owning runner's preflight wipes any stray provisioned row (team_membership first, then app_user, by subject) — safe by construction because she is reserved. Bonus: the same preflight is where E-pre least-privilege assertions live (mint the service-account token, read must 200, create/update/delete must each 403, abort red otherwise) — turning a one-time manual security proof into a committed gate. The no-oracle contract means 'directory off' is invisible at the endpoint; the preflight discriminates via the service-account grant + a search for the realm-guaranteed reserved account.

name: Second service in the local rig + runtime-bootstrap e2e for app-resolved roles
description: Adding a SECOND example service (user-management) to the deploy.sh container-pool rig: a focused infra/compose.usermgmt.yaml (the service + its OWN Postgres on a fresh host port) added under an ENABLE_USER_SERVICE toggle that also flips the catalog pods to CATALOG_ROLE_SOURCE=http + the in-network base URL (http://usermgmt:8080). The user-service dogfoods the starter, so its team.rego must be COPIED into the shared OPA's mounted policy dir (infra/opa/policies/) — the service's own resources/opa/policies/ is the source of truth; restart OPA after editing (--watch doesn't always reload, mx-4e1191). The e2e challenge: the team-target catalog id and the IdP subjects are only known at run time, so a static seed can't wire the demo data. Solution: a small idempotent INTERNAL bootstrap surface (/internal/bootstrap/{users,teams,custom-roles,memberships}) mounted under the already-permitAll /internal/** path (in-network only, NOT the public secured management API), plus a run-team-matrix.sh that mints four in-network tokens, base64url-decodes each JWT 'sub', seeds a fixed demo catalog row into the catalog DB (the stable team-target), bootstraps the team+memberships through the internal API, then runs newman. Proves through the gateway: owner writes / viewer-member denied / custom-editor (team-scoped custom role) writes / non-member denied — roles resolved from real membership — plus the dogfood management path (owner manages, member 403). Keep the bootstrap clearly scoped as test scaffolding so the secured management API stays the demonstrated path.

Live e2e filter-matrix run surfaced two issues the unit/IT tests (synthetic role-defs) could not: (1) the demo's allow-all category lister bound to the SYSTEM owner role got an EMPTY list; (2) reruns drifted the row counts.
resolution: (1) The system 'owner' role resolves to {permissions:{catalog:[read,write]}} — it has NO 'category' key. The Phase-5 'filter' rule checks '"read" in permissions[input.resource.type]' with resource.type='category', so under the system owner the residual is DENY_ALL -> empty list. This is CORRECT (catalog-verbs != category-verbs in the role model), not a filter bug. Fix the DEMO: give the allow-all subject a custom 'curator' role with ungated category:[read,write] (no requiredTags -> ALLOW_ALL residual on categories). Lesson: an 'allow-all over type X' subject needs a role that actually grants verbs on type X; a parent-type grant doesn't cascade to child-type list filtering. (2) The create-category endpoint isn't idempotent, so the matrix must DELETE the demo catalog's categories before seeding (DELETE FROM category WHERE catalog_id=...) — otherwise reruns accumulate rows and 'exactly N' assertions drift. With the clean seed the matrix is stable across reruns (16/16, verified 3x). BONUS newman gotcha: inject runtime ids via --env-var (environment scope) but read them in test scripts with pm.variables.get() (resolves across scopes) NOT pm.collectionVariables.get() (collection scope only — sees the empty declared default); and don't declare the ids as collection variables at all (their empty default shadows nothing but is noise).

description: E2E hierarchy matrix failed only on a long-lived rig: its 'foreign' catalog fixture id (4444) is the hierarchy-LIST matrix's GRANTED root, and the user-service DB persists across runs — a stale team from a past list-matrix run granted the same viewer reader an inheritable role on 4444, flipping the re-parent 403 assert into a policy-correct 200. Looked exactly like a library regression after a redeploy; the library was right, the fixtures were poisoned.
resolution: Fixture-id discipline across matrices: an id one matrix uses as a NEGATIVE case must never be an id another matrix GRANTS on (registry now in scripts/postman/README.md; hierarchy-foreign moved to 6666). When an e2e negative-case assert fails on a long-lived rig, check the persistent usermgmt teams for stale grants on the fixture id BEFORE suspecting the code: SELECT ... FROM team WHERE target_id LIKE '<id-prefix>%'.

name: e2e list-filtering matrix: two subjects, same endpoint, different row sets through the gateway
description: The Phase-5 data-filtering e2e (run-filter-matrix.sh + data-filter-matrix.postman_collection.json), modeled on run-tag-matrix.sh but asserting LIST row SETS not single 200/403. Needs the full rig ENABLE_OIDC=1 ENABLE_USER_SERVICE=1 ./deploy.sh up --pods 2. At run time: mint in-network tokens (issuer keycloak:8888 caveat) for owner(editor)/reader-emea(viewer)/reader-apac(demo)/stranger(OUTSIDER — the rig's standing unbound user, also run-team-matrix.sh's non-member); seed a fixed demo catalog row (the team-target) via psql into opa-abac-postgres; via the user-service /internal/bootstrap/* create a team + two single-region-gated custom roles (emea-reader requiredTags region ANY_OF [emea]; apac-reader [apac]) + bind owner->owner, the two readers->their gated roles, and DELIBERATELY leave the stranger UNBOUND (no membership -> no role definition); create three region-tagged Categories (emea/apac/amer) through the gateway with the owner token; run newman. The 4 list assertions on GET /catalogs/{id}/categories: reader-emea sees ONLY the emea row (1), reader-apac ONLY apac (1, a DIFFERENT set — the decisive proof the residual is in SQL not a post-filter), owner ALL three, stranger [] (the fail-closed boundary: filter rule has no subject-roles fallback). GOTCHAS: (1) deploy.sh only rebuilds the app image if it's ABSENT (image_exists || build_image) — after changing app code you MUST run ./deploy.sh build to force a rebuild, else the pods run stale code; (2) ./profile.sh up (base Postgres) must run BEFORE ./deploy.sh up; (3) restart/redeploy OPA after editing category.rego (the rig mounts it but --watch doesn't always reload — confirm via POST /v1/compile that the filter rule is present); (4) keep the runtime-captured category ids in the collection variable scope, NOT the env file (env scope shadows collection -> empty-id URLs). DOC NAMING: the GUIDE note must NOT share a basename with the planning-index note — both were DATA-FILTERING.md (collision); rename the guide to a distinct basename (PARTIAL-EVALUATION-FILTERING) like the TAG-DICTIONARY plan vs TAG-BASED-AUTHORIZATION guide precedent.

name: Suite-wide wire-shape break in newman: scout the blast radius, migrate extraction only, keep every pinned count
description: Migrating every list response from bare array to an envelope across a newman suite (5.95): (1) SCOUT first (a read-only sub-agent sweep): find every test-script line treating a list body as an array (json.map/.length/[0]/Array.isArray + variables storing list bodies) — the 5.95 sweep found only 3 of 7 collections consumed list bodies (8 sites), the rest asserted status only; (2) migrate ONLY the extraction (pm.response.json().map -> pm.response.json().items.map) and keep every pinned numeric expectation numerically identical (1/1/>=3/0) — the cut must not move, only the shape; (3) give the new matrix a DEDICATED fixture set in the fixture-id registry (7777…) because its counts are pinned exactly (5/3) and shared fixtures must not grow; (4) seed catalogs in runner SQL WITH the ltree path (and repair it in the ON CONFLICT arm) — see the broken-lineage failure record. Validation: a sub-agent runs all runners sequentially and reports only failure summaries (8 scripts, 128 assertions).

e2e runner seeds a catalog row via direct SQL without the ltree path column -> the first category creation under it dies 500 with AncestorResolutionException 'parent has no path (broken lineage)' (HierarchicalPathMaintainer fail-closes on NULL parent path, by design since 5.5-A). Pre-5.5-A fixture rows were backfilled by the adoption migration, so OLD matrices never trip this — only NEW direct-SQL seeds do (discovered in the 5.95 pagination matrix). The json_field id extraction then KeyErrors under set -euo pipefail before the friendly error prints, so the symptom is a bare python Traceback.
resolution: Seed catalogs the run-hierarchy-matrix.sh way: INSERT ... (tags, path) VALUES (..., CAST('catalog_' || replace('<uuid>','-','') AS ltree)) and make the conflict arm repair it too: ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name, path = EXCLUDED.path (a prior failed run leaves a NULL-path row behind). CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS ltree first.

description: An e2e gateway assertion can PASS without exercising the feature under test (CUT). The hierarchy matrix's 'inheritance -> 200' check seeded the reader role with BOTH catalog:[read] AND category:[read]; since category.rego decides allow via 'granted if direct_grant' where direct_grant = verb in permissions[resource.type], the direct category:read fired and the 200 proved a DIRECT grant — the test would still pass if the new inherited_grant clause + the inheritable data file were deleted. The rego UNIT test correctly isolated inheritance (a catalog-ONLY role) but the e2e did not. This is the 'asserts shape (200) not the cut (inheritance-vs-direct)' agentic-laziness failure mode the autonomous-run lens watches for.
resolution: Seed the e2e so the asserted outcome can ONLY come from the CUT: give the reader catalog:[read] ONLY (no direct category grant), so a readable Category proves inherited_grant. Verify by reading back the seeded role from the user-mgmt DB (here: {"catalog":["read"]}). General rule for allow/deny matrices: the role/tag seed must make the decisive request's success attributable to the new clause alone — mirror how the rego unit test isolates it, don't grant a superset that lets the old direct path satisfy the assertion.

description: Newman e2e chain broke: every request after 'create catalog' hit /catalogs// (empty id) and 404'd, even though the create step set the id via pm.collectionVariables.set('catalog_id', ...). Cause: the chained ids were ALSO declared (empty) in the Postman environment file. Newman resolves {{var}} with environment scope winning over collection scope, so the empty env value shadowed the captured collection value.
resolution: Keep runtime-captured chain ids in the COLLECTION scope only — do not declare catalog_id/category_id/product_id in the environment file. (Or capture them with pm.environment.set instead.) Also: in newman 6, an Auth/token request that run-tests.sh pre-injects can be cleanly skipped with a prerequest pm.execution.skipRequest() guard so it doesn't report a spurious failed request.

description: The Phase-5.5-A deny-overrides control tag (input.resource.attributes.abac_deny == true) cannot be assigned through the catalog gateway's create/update path: the Phase-4.5 TagAssignmentService validates every tag key against the dynamic tag dictionary and rejects an unknown key with 422 'Unknown tag key abac_deny (no applicable definition)'. So the hierarchy e2e's deny-overrides scenario fails at category creation when it tries to POST tags:{abac_deny:true}.
resolution: abac_deny is an OPERATIONAL control flag (a policy deny-override), not a user-facing business tag, so it should not go through dictionary validation. In the e2e, create the Category plainly then set the flag OUT-OF-BAND via SQL: UPDATE category SET tags = jsonb_set(coalesce(tags,'{}'::jsonb),'{abac_deny}','true') WHERE id=... (the same way the matrix seeds catalogs). For a real deployment, either register abac_deny as a reserved/system tag key in the dictionary, or carry the deny flag on a dedicated column instead of the JSONB tags. Also: make e2e create helpers surface the raw response on a non-id body (don't pipe straight into a python ['id'] that throws a bare KeyError traceback).

name: A newman collection AS an MCP client: the three framings, and why the drills belong to the runner
description: scripts/postman/agent-tool-matrix.postman_collection.json drives a streamable-HTTP MCP server end to end with nothing but Postman scripts - no SDK, no node client. THE FRAMING IS NOT UNIFORM ON ONE ENDPOINT, which is what breaks a naive script: (a) POST /mcp initialize answers PLAIN application/json and assigns Mcp-Session-Id as a RESPONSE HEADER (capture with pm.response.headers.get); (b) a JSON-RPC NOTIFICATION (no id, e.g. notifications/initialized) answers 202 with an EMPTY BODY - a script that parses it fails on a CORRECT server; (c) every later REQUEST (tools/list, tools/call) is SSE-framed (text/event-stream, 'data:' lines) on that same endpoint. Later requests must carry mcp-session-id (transport-enforced) + MCP-Protocol-Version. Assert all three framings explicitly so an SDK bump fails HERE rather than somewhere subtler. SHARING PARSE HELPERS: Postman has no module system - put the helper source in a collection-level prerequest script as an ARRAY OF JS STRING LITERALS joined with String.fromCharCode(10) into a collection variable, then eval(pm.collectionVariables.get('mcpHelpers')) per test. Do NOT use a template literal for this: inside backticks a \n escape becomes a real newline and the stored source no longer parses. Generate the JSON from a throwaway builder if hand-escaping JS-in-JSON-in-a-JS-string is error-prone. FOLDER-PER-CELL + --folder is what makes rig DRILLS possible: cells that need the rig mutated mid-suite (stop the PDP, recreate the pod with a kill-switch off, recreate it with a capability emptied) cannot be collection steps, so each is its own self-handshaking folder the RUNNER invokes between mutations. Give the runner an EXIT trap that restores the rig (PDP up, pod on its default profile) however the run ends - without it a failed drill leaves the next run, and the demo UI, silently different. Make the mutable knobs compose-interpolated (${VAR-default}, the bare dash so an explicitly EMPTY value stays empty) rather than hardcoded.

SYMPTOM (historical, FIXED 2026-07-31): during an E9 'every pre-existing runner re-runs green' sweep, run-tests.sh (the catalog lifecycle collection) and run-matrix.sh (the role-based abac matrix) both failed with 'create catalog -> 201, then GET/child-create on it -> 403', while all 12 other runners passed. Looked exactly like a regression from whatever slice was in flight; it was not.
resolution: ROOT CAUSE: both suites CREATE their own catalog, and Slice B4 (ADR 0018) made MEMBERSHIP THE SOLE ACCESS PATH - so on the user-service rig (CATALOG_ROLE_SOURCE=http) a freshly created, team-less catalog is unreachable EVEN BY ITS CREATOR. Neither collection bound a team; they were last touched 2026-06-12, B4 landed 2026-06-29/30, so they had been rig-flavour-locked for a month and every subsequent slice rediscovered it during its own E9 sweep. FIXED 2026-07-31: both collections now claim their catalog with a self-service team (the SHIPPED public POST /api/v1/teams, owner-on-create) and the abac matrix binds its viewer to that team as a 'reader' - so the same 200/403 contrast is now decided by REAL MEMBERSHIP. The bootstrap steps guard themselves with pm.execution.skipRequest() (works in newman 6.2.1) on a b4_bootstrap env var the runner sets. Green on BOTH flavours: user-service 22 + 21 assertions, OIDC-only 19 + 19. THE DETECTION TRAP, worth more than the fix: probe the CATALOG POD's own CATALOG_ROLE_SOURCE (docker inspect; default 'demo' when absent, matching application.yml), NOT whether the user-service is reachable - 'ENABLE_OIDC=1 ./deploy.sh up' recreates the catalog pods on the static supplier but LEAVES AN ALREADY-RUNNING usermgmt CONTAINER ALONE, so a reachability probe reports 'membership rig' on a rig that ignores membership entirely, the bootstrap runs, creates a team nobody consults, and the suite passes for the wrong reason. Caught only because the skip path was verified explicitly rather than assumed. E9 still needs THREE rig passes overall, now only because run-resilience-matrix.sh is rig-exclusive (it repoints role resolution at the fault stub).

description: SYMPTOM (design smell, found by deep review): an e2e runner aborts with exit 1 on a 'git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD' invariant — 'this branch changed the library, so the target layer is no longer as shipped'. It reads like a rigorous guard and passes on the branch that wrote it.
resolution: A test runner must assert RIG state, not REPOSITORY state. A VCS-derived assertion is a fact about the branch, not about the run, so it turns into a false failure the moment a LATER slice legitimately touches the guarded paths — and the failure names something unrelated to whatever that slice is testing. Downgrade such checks to a printed WARNING (keep the check, drop the exit), or move them into the review/clean-room gate where branch-scoped assertions belong. Behavioural greps over the code under test (e.g. 'the outbound client sets exactly Authorization + Accept') can stay HARD: they assert a property of the shipped code the e2e is exercising, and a refactor that breaks them genuinely invalidates the run. Also parameterize the base ref (SHIPPED_BASE=origin/main) so a fork or a detached checkout does not trip it.

name: A derived-scope e2e must assert exact ids + a NEGATIVE id, and the outage cell must prove CONFINEMENT not just the degrade
description: Building the e2e for a scope DERIVED from a relation (SUPERVISED-SCOPE: a manager's reach derived from reporting edges through their reports' CONTROL-capable team seats). Four things make the difference between a matrix that proves the feature and one that passes for the wrong reason. (1) EXACT IDS *AND* AN EXACT COUNT, never one or the other: a widened derivation fails on the count, a narrowed one on the ids - either alone lets the other through. (2) A NEGATIVE ID INSIDE THE HEADLINE CELL: the headline persona's assertion must include an id that must NOT appear for a stated reason (here a report's READER seat, since reach is CONTROL-capable seats only). Without it the reach RULE is asserted nowhere at rig level, and its violation is the silent widening - one report's unrelated seat pulling their manager into another unit. It costs one extra fixture catalog. (3) PROBE THE RUNTIME SHAPE, not the convenient one: the contents-are-closed cell must be requested with the ancestor chain PRESENT (through the gateway, on a real nested resource), because the same probe without ancestors returns false for the wrong reason - which is exactly how a live inheritance fail-open got green-lit in planning (ADR 0031 Context). (4) THE OUTAGE CELL NEEDS A SECOND SUBJECT. 'Fault the edge, the supervisor sees only their own memberships' is unfalsifiable for a PURE supervisor, whose own-memberships floor is the empty page - identical to 'the whole user-service is down'. Add a cell asserting an ordinary MEMBER's page is UNCHANGED during the same fault: that is the only assertion that makes a dedicated per-edge base-URL and a dedicated breaker observable from outside, and without it a shared resolve breaker would still pass. RELATED ORDERING RULE: a cell that MUTATES the relation (removing an edge to prove liveness) goes LAST in the collection and the description says so, since every earlier cell depends on the original graph; and the runner must SELF-RESET before seeding, because such a matrix is deliberately not idempotent. Reserve the whole persona FAMILY in the fixture registry, not just catalog ids: a derived set is transitive, so one stray membership on any '\''report'\'' account silently widens the manager's page and breaks the exact-count assertion (relates to mx-271e72, which reserved a single subject for the same class of reason).

Vacuous newman deny cells: pm.test('...', () => pm.response.code === N) passes UNCONDITIONALLY — newman ignores a returned boolean; pm.test fails only when the callback throws. 39 cells across 4 collections (supervised-scope 18, isolation 11, data-filter 8, hierarchy-list 2) asserted nothing, including the isolation E6 deep-link/E7 squat denials and the whole supervised read-only-ceiling/contents-closed cut. The collection-level green (0 failed) was therefore not evidence for any of those cells. Found by the SUPERVISED-SCOPE layer-3 adversarial review; proven empirically with a 200-returning probe server (only the to.have.status form fails).
resolution: Rewrote all 39 to () => pm.response.to.have.status(N) and re-ran the four matrices live — all deny cells genuinely hold (instrument debt, not enforcement failure). Convention now pinned in docs/guides/E2E-TESTING.md (assertion-style: callbacks must throw; bare top-level pm.expect is the inverse smell — wrap in a named pm.test). Grep for the class: '=> pm.response.code ===' (arrow form only; if-conditionals are legitimate).

name: The E6-flip: a later slice deliberately rewriting an earlier matrix's cells, and sharing its reserved persona family
description: PRODUCTION-TIER T6 rewrote three cells of SUPERVISED-SCOPE's shipped matrix (contents-closed 403 -> contents-open 200) because slice B changed exactly the behavior slice A had pinned as its boundary. Four things make that safe instead of a regression-shaped red run. (1) PLAN THE FLIP IN THE DECOMPOSITION, so the run never 'discovers' a red matrix mid-e2e: name the cells, the new contract, and where the old proof MOVES to. (2) FLIP, NEVER DELETE — and say so in the cell's own comment: the closed-contents proof moved to the new matrix (production + unproven + the tier-flip liveness cell), and the rewritten cell points at its new owner by filename, so a future reader finding an old doc that promises 'contents are closed' reads it as the earlier slice's boundary rather than a regression. (3) UPGRADE THE FLIPPED CELL WHILE YOU ARE THERE: A's cells asserted only a status code; the flipped versions assert exact ids + count, so the rewrite makes the matrix stronger, not merely different. (4) SWEEP THE PROSE THAT PINNED THE OLD CONTRACT — scripts/postman/README.md's per-runner row and the runner's own header comment both stated 'E6 contents closed ... each 403'; a flip that leaves either behind ships a self-contradicting doc. SHARED-PERSONA COROLLARY: B needed a supervised decision, so it needed a reporting edge for sup-anna, whose whole family the A matrix reserves ('no other matrix may add a reporting edge for them'). Minting a second supervisor would have been a realm diff the slice forbade, so the rule got a NARROW, WRITTEN exception plus the two mechanical rules that make sharing safe: (a) every runner DELETES the edges it manages before seeding, so whichever runs second starts from its own org; (b) the newcomer binds NO account from the reserved family into its own teams (B's teams are owned by the shared `editor` seeder account), so nothing it leaves behind can widen the reserved manager's page and break the owner matrix's exact-id cell. Verify by running both matrices back to back IN BOTH ORDERS, not just once.

read -r A B <<<"$(fn)" SWALLOWS the function's exit 1 (PRODUCTION-TIER layer-3): a runner's fixture-seed guard did 'exit 1' inside a command substitution consumed by a herestring read. The exit terminates only the substitution subshell; the herestring then feeds read a bare newline, read returns 0, and set -euo pipefail never fires — so a failed seed sailed into newman as a wall of 404/403 assertion noise instead of stopping at the real cause. Reproduced on this machine's bash 3.2: 'ERROR...' printed, rc_of_read_line=0, next line ran, script exit 0.
resolution: Assignment-then-read: pair="$(fn)" || exit 1; [ -n "$pair" ] || exit 1; read -r A B <<<"$pair". The assignment form propagates the substitution's exit status (the herestring form does not); the non-empty check catches a silent empty print. Sweep every 'read <<<"$(' in scripts/postman when touching a runner.
